title: The Brave Little Seed
summary: A tiny seed is afraid of the dark under the ground. To grow, she'll have to climb all the way up to the light.

scenes.text:
Under the ground, deep down, lived a tiny little seed.

Everything down there was dark. Dark and quiet. You couldn't see anything, not up, not down, not to the sides.

Sometimes, from very far away, sounds came down from the world above. Footsteps. Children laughing. A bird singing. But they arrived so muffled, so covered up by the earth, that the seed didn't know whether they were real or whether she was dreaming them.

"What if I stay down here for ever?" she thought, curled up in her shell.

She was scared of staying. But she was even more scared of going up.

One morning, it began to rain.

The water trickled slowly down through the earth, drop by drop, until it reached the seed and soaked her right through.

The seed drank. And drank. And she began to feel something new, like a tickle inside. A great big wish to stretch.

She stretched a tiny bit.

And her shell went: crack!

Out of the little split came a thin white root, which dug down into the earth, like someone dropping an anchor.

After a while, a worm came by.

"Good morning," he said. "My name's Wormy. Why are you keeping so still?"

"I'm scared," said the seed. "My root has come out downwards. But now I'm supposed to grow upwards, and up there it's all dark. I don't know what's there."

Wormy laughed with his whole tail.

"Dark? It isn't dark up there. Up there is the light. I saw it once, when I came out after the rain. It's warm, and yellow, and it smells of morning."

"And how do I get there?"

"Slowly," said Wormy. "Like everything worth doing."

The seed gathered up all her courage.

And she pushed a little green arm upwards.

She pushed, and pushed, and pushed. The earth was heavy, but the shoot was stubborn.

Halfway up she came to a stone, big and hard. She couldn't get through it. So, very patiently, she went round it, bit by bit, until she had squeezed past.

And then she saw it.

High above, through a gap in the earth, came a thread of light.

The seed didn't think twice. She took a deep breath, and kept climbing towards it.

And suddenly, out she came!

Her little green leaf popped up above the earth, and the first thing she felt was the sun on her face. Warm. Yellow. Smelling of morning.

Wormy was right.

All around there was grass, and flowers, and an enormous blue sky. The birds were singing. The air waved her little leaf from side to side, as if it were saying hello.

"I did it!" shouted the seed, who wasn't a seed any more, but a plant.

And out came a giggle, as green and as new as she was.

Many days went by, and many rains, and many suns.

The tiny plant grew into a big tree, with branches that hugged the sky. Children played in her shade. Birds built nests among her leaves.

And one autumn day, a tiny seed came loose from one of her branches. It fell to the ground, and slowly drifted off to sleep down below, in the dark.

The tree leaned down towards it a little. And she whispered, very softly:

"Don't be scared. There's light up here. I'll be waiting for you."
